gloss: suddenly, abruptly, out of the blue

definitions.explanation: Describes something happening unexpectedly and without preparation or build-up.

examples.japanese: いきなり{来|き}ないでよ。
examples.english: Don't just show up out of nowhere.

examples.japanese: いきなり{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ってきた。
いきなり{怒|おこ}り{出|だ}してびっくりした。
examples.english: I was surprised when they suddenly got angry.

examples.japanese: いきなり{難|むずか}しいことを{言|い}われても{困|こま}る。
examples.english: I'm stumped when you suddenly ask something difficult.

notes:
いきなり emphasizes the unexpected, abrupt nature of an action or event. It often implies that something happened without the usual preparation, warning, or gradual lead-up.

Common collocations:
- いきなり{来|く}る: to show up suddenly
- いきなり{始|はじ}まる: to start abruptly
- いきなり{言|い}う: to say out of nowhere

Similar expressions:
- {突然|とつぜん}: suddenly (more neutral/formal)
- {急|きゅう}に: suddenly (emphasizes speed)
- だしぬけに: unexpectedly, out of the blue
